# YM10: 坦坦荡荡 Tantan Dangdang, "Tranquil and Vast"

Malone calls it The Tank.

Wave 2 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM10` · Page: `/scenes/#YM10` · Row: `research/buildings/YM10-tantan-dangdang/`

## What it was

坦坦荡荡 Tantan Dangdang, the fish-pond scene on the west shore of the Back Lake, earlier called 鱼池 'the fish pond' (S05 j81:2b; the old name only in a search extract). S05: a three-bay 坦坦荡荡 hall, 素心堂 Suxin Tang as the front hall, 光风霁月 Guangfeng Jiyue as the rear hall, 知鱼亭 Zhiyu Ting to the north-east, 萃景斋 Cuijing Zhai further north-east and 双佳斋 Shuangjia Zhai to the north-west (S05 j81:2b). The editors of S361 read the layout as a five-bay gate hall 素心堂 with an annex, 半亩园 Banmu Yuan east, 澹怀堂 west, and the five-bay 光风霁月 standing in the middle of the pool (E1333). Malone too places 光风霁月 in mid-tank, bridged on all four sides (E1332, S02). Daoguang still dined with the dowager at 半亩园 in 1839 (E1328, S360). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).

From the inventory row: **built** 康熙后叶 初称金鱼池; 定名 乾隆四年 1739 (S42); late Kangxi, as 金鱼池; named 1739; **changed** Pool reshaped from 卍 to a rectangle shortly before 1744 (S41); **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S08, S41, S42, S01, S340).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Preface of 1744: "鑿池為魚樂國池周舍下錦鱗數千頭" (S05 j81:3a). A pool was dug as a 'kingdom of happy fish' with thousands of brocade-scaled fish around and under the buildings; the poem turns Zhuangzi's 'joy of fish' into the ruler's concern for his people (我蒿目乎斯民). The poem was also cut on a rock at 萃景斋 (S05 j81:3a).

### How later sources differ

S05 lists six names; S360 adds 碧澜亭 Bilan Ting (poems 1764-1795, E1331) and 半亩园 (in use 1839, E1328), and the plan S01 labels the main hall '坦:荡:' on a 15-cell row (YM10-01): the scene grew east and west after 1744. 素心堂 has poems to 1819 (E1329).

## What survives today

Excavated from spring 2003, with 碧澜桥 Bilan Qiao and five other bridges; design drawings for presenting 坦坦荡荡 and the bridges 如意桥, 南大桥, 棕亭桥, 鸣溪桥, the one-arch bridge of 慈云普护 and 碧澜桥 were approved in 2007 (S981). The dig gave a blue-and-white porcelain stool from the 'goldfish pond' 金鱼池, restored in the 修复1860 project (E1339, S334). The pool and footings are shown in the park today; the dig report itself was not reached.
